page: Microsoft Azure D96ls_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Dlsv7 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor with x86_64 architecture. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz and includes a 480 MB L3 cache. The system is configured with 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, though it is Premium Storage capable.

In benchmark evaluations, the D96ls_v7 demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities and high instruction throughput. The processor support for Advanced Vector Extensions and Advanced Matrix Extensions contributes to top-tier performance in specialized tasks, as evidenced by a Passmark CPU extended instructions score of 119233.71 and a Geekbench ray tracing score of 102598.0. Single-threaded performance is also notable, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2224.0 and a gzip compression rate of 36.54 GB/sec. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 575.95 GB/sec, while Redis SET operations achieve 151.03 million operations per second.

The server hardware profile presents a clear tradeoff, prioritizing raw compute density and high clock speeds over memory capacity and local storage. With only 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU and no local NVMe drives, it is highly cost-efficient for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive in-memory datasets. It is well-suited for software compilation, static web serving, and medium-sized LLM inference tasks, such as 7B model prompt processing.
description: The Microsoft Azure D96ls_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine from the Dlsv7 family, powered by a 96-vCPU Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running at 4.2 GHz on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Featuring 192.0 GB of RAM and no local storage, this server is designed for high-throughput compute tasks. It delivers exceptional multi-core performance, highlighted by a Passmark CPU score of 104787.21 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression speed of 575.95 GB/sec. The processor includes advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and Intel AMX, which accelerate cryptographic and matrix operations. While its low memory-to-vCPU ratio represents a tradeoff for memory-intensive applications, its high compute density makes it highly cost-efficient for CPU-bound workloads. It is ideal for software compilation, static web serving, and medium-scale LLM inference.
